newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Bank sees slower total loan growth.
newsitem.headline: DBS Bank sees slower total loan growth.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore Ltd said on Thursday it expects slower total bank loan growth in 1997, but still anticipated double digit percentage growth.
DBS Bank President Ng Kee Choe told reporters at a briefing after the release of 1996 results that total bank loan growth had been around 16 percent in 1996.

"For 1997, we also expect double digit growth in loans in the same order of magnitude or slightly slower," Ng said. He added that he expected loan growth to be slower but declined to give further details.
Banking analysts have previously said they expected total Singapore bank loan growth of 12 to 13 percent in 1997.
